name: Adrasteia
description: One of the three spinning Fates of Theros, who cuts the threads of mortals whose lives have finished.

description_citations.text: "Adrasteia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Adrasteia prepares to cut a snarl in the tapestry where a blue and a gold thread have intertwined.
timeline.quote: Two threads, one blue, the other gold, which had begun their journey through the tapestry in parallel, had now become intertwined.

citation.text: "Emonberry Red" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Adrasteia's shears take the snarl and the tip of her thumb, and a drop of her blood stains the tapestry.
timeline.quote: The shears took the snarl, and along with it the very tip of her thumb.

citation.text: "Emonberry Red" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Feb 2014.

timeline.summary: Adrasteia notices a snarl of two intertwined threads, one blue and one gold, in the weave of the Fates.
timeline.quote: At one point, Adrasteia noticed a particularly large snarl of threads in the weave of the Fates.

citation.text: "Adrasteia", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Adrasteia decides one thread cannot be saved without harming the other, since their destinies are bound together.
timeline.quote: One without the other could weaken the tapestry, leaving it prone to irreparable tears.

citation.text: "Adrasteia", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Adrasteia takes out her crooked black shears from a box beneath the table.
timeline.quote: The shears could never be fully closed.

citation.text: "Adrasteia", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Adrasteia misjudges her snip and cuts off the tip of her thumb, staining the tapestry with a drop of her blood.
timeline.quote: The shears took the snarl, and along with it the very tip of her thumb.

citation.text: "Adrasteia", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

relations.note: He offered to forge her a new set of shears.
relations.quote: Purphoros had offered to forge her a new set long ago

citation.text: "Emonberry Red" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Feb 2014.

relations.quote: Purphoros had offered to forge her a new set long ago

pages_say.description: One of three weaver sisters of fate, detached and efficient, who snips a snarl of two entwined threads with her crooked shears.

citation.text: "Emonberry Red" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 5 Feb 2014.
